egress.terms: "Traffic: Unlimited *" on every tier, and "Each Storage Box comes with unlimited traffic" (docs). The asterisk is a real fair-use clause: a documented 2022 enforcement email told a customer "your traffic use, which currently averages above 250 TB/month ... is far above what we consider fair use." The 250 TB/month in that email is the only threshold Hetzner has ever enforced.

interface_detail: SFTP, SCP, rsync, FTPS, SMB/CIFS, WebDAV, BorgBackup, SSH (port 23); 100 sub-accounts; 10 concurrent connections
tooling: No S3 endpoint — this is the one real gap. rclone via SFTP or WebDAV; Borg/restic first-class
chaining: WebDAV -> AList -> Cloudflare works. 100 sub-accounts let you hand one directory each to separate services.
limits_note: 10 concurrent connections is the ceiling on parallel reads; there is no S3 object API, so no presigned URLs, and every read runs through WebDAV, SFTP or rsync
reliability_note: Cost: aggressive new-account KYC. LET threads document ID-card scans being requested and accounts silently refused for country/risk reasons; UnionPay accepted but does not waive KYC.
